MUQATIL:12:48-51/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r3.claim: Joseph asks the king's messenger to investigate the five women who cut their fingers, because he wants his innocence established before leaving prison rather than remaining suspect.

TAB-FULL:v13p198/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r1.claim: After the messenger reported Joseph’s interpretation, the king recognized its truth and ordered that Joseph be brought to him.

TAB-FULL:v13p198/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that the messenger told the king Joseph’s interpretation, which matched what was in the king’s mind, so the king summoned him.

TAB-FULL:v13p198/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p198/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says that when the king’s messenger came, the king ordered Joseph brought to him.

TAB-FULL:v13p199/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r1.claim: Joseph refuses to leave with the messenger until the king establishes the truth about the women’s accusation and the affair that led to his imprisonment.

TAB-FULL:v13p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Joseph also asked the king to investigate the woman whose affair had caused his imprisonment.

TAB-FULL:v13p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r3.claim: Al-Suddi recounts that Joseph declined the summons and sent the king back to ask about the women who cut their hands.

TAB-FULL:v13p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that leaving before the king learned the facts would have left the Aziz suspicious that Joseph had pursued his wife.

TAB-FULL:v13p199/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p199/r5.claim: The Prophet praised Joseph’s deliberation, saying that he would have answered the summons quickly if he had been imprisoned and called.

TAB-FULL:v13p202/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r1.claim: The Prophet says he would have answered quickly and sought no excuse if summoned from prison, unlike Joseph’s deliberate request for an inquiry.

TAB-FULL:v13p202/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet admires Joseph’s patience and generosity; he would have demanded release before interpreting and rushed to the door when called, while Joseph sought exoneration.

TAB-FULL:v13p202/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r3.claim: Qatada says the Prophet wanted Joseph to secure his exoneration before leaving prison.

TAB-FULL:v13p202/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v13p202/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Joseph wanted an excuse established before he left prison.

TAB-FULL:v13p203/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p203/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p203/r1.claim: God knows the women’s schemes and deeds against Joseph and others, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will requite them.

TAB-FULL:v13p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p203/r2.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v13p203/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation takes “my lord” as the Aziz, Iṭfīr, who knows that Joseph is innocent of the accusation.

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r6.claim: In ‘return to your lord,’ lord means the king, the master or owner of someone.

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r7.claim: Al-lāʾī may replace allātī for ‘the women’; Joseph asks the king to establish that he is innocent of the accusation.

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r8.speaker: النبي
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet admired Joseph’s restraint: had he been in Joseph’s place, he would have hastened to respond to the king’s summons rather than first seeking proof of innocence.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r1.claim: When the king's messenger ordered Joseph to come, Joseph refused to leave and sent him back to his master.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r2.claim: The Prophet said that had he been Joseph, he would have hurried to answer the summons rather than seek an excuse.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2155/r3.claim: The Prophet marveled at Joseph's patience and generosity and said he himself would have hurried to the door; Joseph sought to be vindicated by asking about the women.

NAHHAS:v2p331/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p331/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p331/r3.claim: Joseph asks the king to investigate the women to show he was jailed without wrongdoing, demonstrating their plot.

THALABI:v5p228/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p228/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p228/r1.claim: After the cupbearer relayed Joseph’s interpretation, the king realized it would come true and summoned its interpreter.

THALABI:v5p228/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p228/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p228/r2.claim: Joseph refused to leave prison with the messenger until his innocence was established, asking the king to investigate the women who cut their hands.

THALABI:v5p228/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p228/r3.speaker: عاصم
THALABI:v5p228/r3.claim: A transmission from Abu Bakr ibn Abbas says Asim read al-niswah with a rounded initial nūn.

THALABI:v5p228/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p228/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p228/r4.claim: Joseph says God knows the women’s plotting; an alternative takes my lord as the Aziz, who knows Joseph is innocent of the accusation.

THALABI:v5p228/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p228/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p228/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph was brought out before the king had cleared the matter to his own satisfaction; the Aziz still suspected him of tempting his wife.

THALABI:v5p229/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p229/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p229/r1.claim: The Prophet admires Joseph’s patience: he would have demanded release before interpreting the king’s dream and would have hurried out when summoned, while Joseph waited to clear his name.

THALABI:v5p230#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p230#2/r1.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v5p230#2/r1.claim: Wahb says the king spoke seventy languages and Yusuf answered each in that language; Yusuf was thirty, impressing the king with his knowledge of the dream.

THALABI:v5p230#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p230#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p230#2/r2.claim: The king asked Yusuf to recount the dream orally, and Yusuf described the seven fat cows, seven gaunt cows, and seven green and black ears of grain.

THALABI:v5p230#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p230#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p230#2/r3.claim: Yusuf recommends sowing abundantly in the fertile years and storing the harvest in its stalks, which can also feed animals.

THALABI:v5p230#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p230#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p230#2/r4.claim: He advises collecting one fifth of people's food, enough for Egypt and neighboring lands, while visitors buy provisions and enlarge the treasury.

THALABI:v5p230#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p230#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p230#2/r5.claim: When the king asks who can manage the work, Yusuf offers himself to oversee the land's storehouses; the gloss takes the phrase as the king's storehouses.

THALABI:v5p233/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p233/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p233/r1.claim: The poems present Yusuf as a model: patient endurance in prison eventually led him to kingship.

THALABI:v5p233/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p233/r2.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v5p233/r2.claim: A letter to a friend says relief follows fear and grief, and urges him not to despair because God gave Yusuf the storehouses after prison.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r10.claim: He may have asked about the other women because they were witnesses against her.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r11.claim: إن ربي may refer to God, who knows the women's plot.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, ربي may refer to Joseph's master, al-Aziz, who knows their plot.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.claim: The king's command is to bring Joseph.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r6.claim: The messenger who reaches Joseph is sent back to the king; Joseph delays leaving so his innocence is established before appearing, without suspicion of guilt or treachery.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r7.claim: A report through Abu al-Zinad from Abu Hurayra asks God to have mercy on Joseph for his patience and says that the Prophet would have left prison immediately; no grading is stated.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r8.claim: Joseph may have omitted naming the ruler's wife because doing so could cast suspicion on her.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45#2/r9.claim: He may have spared her reputation because she was married to the king.

QUSHAYRI:v2p80/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p80/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p80/r1.claim: Joseph waited for the king to see his innocence so the king would not suspect him and discount his words.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r1.claim: Joseph refused to leave immediately with the messenger and asked him to return to the king to inquire about the women who had cut their hands, so his innocence would be established.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r2.claim: بال means a state or affair; Joseph asked the king to investigate the women's case and establish his innocence from the false accusation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r3.claim: Joseph asked the king to establish his innocence and show he had been imprisoned unjustly without committing a crime.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r4.claim: Qatāda says Joseph sought an excuse or acquittal.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r5.claim: The wording omits “ask” or “investigate” before “what was the matter with the women,” because that meaning is already implied.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r6.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r6.claim: Joseph feared the king would still regard him as a suspect in an indecent act and wanted his innocence confirmed before appearing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r7.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r7.claim: The Prophet praised Joseph's composure and patience, saying he would have left immediately if he had been imprisoned and summoned.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p144/r8.claim: Joseph did not single out the governor's wife, showing good manners by including her among the women.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p146/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p146/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p146/r1.claim: God knows the women's plot and can make Joseph's innocence apparent to the king who summoned him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r6.claim: After the royal messenger summoned him, Joseph requested an inquiry into the women so the king would learn he had been jailed unjustly and was innocent.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r7.claim: The women already knew Joseph was innocent because the ruler's wife had confessed before them that she tried to seduce him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r8.claim: Joseph wanted the king to know he had been imprisoned wrongfully; God knew the women's schemes and the king summoned them.

JISHUMI:v5p3659/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3659/r1.speaker: عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3659/r1.claim: In one transmission, ʿĀṣim reads النسوة with ḍamma on nūn; the other readers use kasra, and both are dialects.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r1.claim: After the cupbearer reported Joseph’s interpretation, the king recognized its truth and ordered Joseph brought to him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r2.claim: Joseph refused to leave with the messenger before his innocence was established and asked him to return to the king; he courteously avoided naming the Aziz’s wife directly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r3.claim: The Prophet said he would have answered the caller had he remained imprisoned as long as Joseph.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#3/r4.claim: Joseph says God knows their scheme; he wants the king to receive him after suspicion has been removed.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r1.claim: Yusuf delays answering the king until the women's role is investigated, clearing his name so rivals cannot use his long imprisonment to lower his standing.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r2.claim: The episode supports a duty to avoid suspicion and the places that give rise to it; a prophetic report warns believers not to stand in places of accusation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r3.claim: A prophetic example has Muḥammad identify the woman accompanying him at night to passersby, preventing suspicion.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r4.claim: A report marvels at Yusuf's patience: the Prophet says he would have conditioned his interpretation on release and, after so long, would have hurried out when summoned.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r5.claim: Yusuf asks the king to inquire about the women's affair because a question will prompt a thorough search and expose the story clearly.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r6.claim: Yusuf's graciousness and good manners appear in sparing the Aziz's wife from mention and referring only to the women who cut their hands.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p450/r7.claim: Inna rabbī means God; His knowledge of their plot may describe its depth, witness to their plotting and Yusuf's innocence, or threaten requital.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r1.claim: The passage omits the messenger’s return and report; the king and courtiers admire Joseph’s interpretation and hearing of his truthfulness, increasing his standing.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r2.claim: Joseph asks to learn the women’s case so the king will investigate whether his imprisonment was just; a small part of the story reveals the whole.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r3.claim: He avoids naming the governor’s wife out of good companionship and loyalty to her husband.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿAsim and Abu Ḥaywah read niswah with a ḍamma; others read it with a kasra, both accepted plural forms.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r5.claim: Readers vary between the plural forms اللايي and اللاتي, both derived from التي.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r6.claim: Joseph delays release to secure a public finding of innocence, fearing people would otherwise keep seeing him as the man who pursued his master’s wife.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251#2/r7.claim: A prophetic report praises Joseph’s patience and gentleness and says the Prophet would have answered the call sooner; a route through Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim appears in Bukhari’s tafsir.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r1.claim: The Prophet’s statement is praise for Joseph; the Prophet describes a different but also sound judgment, accepting an earlier release and explaining himself afterward.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r2.claim: These stories guide people facing future trials: delaying a chance to leave prison can lead to indefinite confinement, while Joseph knew by revelation he was safe.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r3.claim: If رب means God, Joseph’s statement that He knows their plotting is a warning and threat.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p252/r4.claim: If رب means his master the governor, Joseph appeals to him and rebukes him; the pronoun in كيدهن refers to the named women in this investigation, not women generally.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r1.claim: After the cupbearer told the king the dream's interpretation, the king believed Joseph and summoned him; Joseph refused to leave before his innocence was established.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r2.claim: Joseph asked the envoy to return to the king and ask what had happened with the women so his innocence would be clear and he would not appear suspected of sexual misconduct.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads al-niswah with a ḍamma on its nūn.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r4.claim: “My Lord knows their guile” most plainly refers to God; al-Tabari reports that Joseph meant his master Aziz, who knew he was innocent.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r5.claim: The Prophet praised Joseph's resolve and patience: had he remained imprisoned as long as Joseph before a summons, he would have answered immediately.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Joseph mentioned the women collectively out of kind treatment and good manners.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r7.claim: The other explanations are that she was a king's wife and Joseph protected her; the women witnessed against her; or naming her alone would invite suspicion.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p236/r8.claim: Another explanation for omitting the wife's name is that she was the king's wife, so Joseph preserved her dignity.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r1.claim: The king valued Joseph's interpretation and ordered him brought; this shows that knowledge frees people from worldly distress and can also free them from afterlife distress.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet praises Joseph's patience and generosity but says the Prophet would have demanded release before interpreting and would have hurried out when summoned.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r3.claim: Joseph wisely refused to leave until the accusation was fully cleared: an immediate release could leave suspicion, while an investigation establishes his innocence and exposes slander.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r4.claim: After twelve years in prison, not rushing out when the king summoned him displayed patience and judgment, making the king regard all accusations as lies.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r5.claim: Requesting inquiry into the women's conduct displayed Joseph's purity, because a guilty man would fear recalling what happened.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.claim: Joseph's refusal to answer the king immediately may have repaired his earlier reliance on the cupbearer: he focused on clearing his name instead of depending on the king's favor.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and al-Kisaʾi read فسله without hamza; the other readers read فاسأله with hamza.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r2.speaker: عاصم، أبو بكر
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r2.claim: Asim through Abu Bakr reads النسوة with a damma on nūn, while the others use kasra; both are dialect forms.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r3.claim: Joseph asks the king to inquire about the women's affair, framing it as a question rather than an order to the king to act.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r4.claim: Joseph does not name the Aziz's wife, despite her role in his imprisonment, and speaks only of the other women.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r5.claim: Though the women may have accused Joseph of shameful conduct, he asks generally about those who cut their hands without detailing or singling out their wrongdoing.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r6.claim: In إن ربي بكيدهن عليم, rabb can mean God, who knows hidden matters, or the king as Joseph's caretaker, implying that the king knows their plot.

RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p122/r7.claim: Their scheming may mean each woman desired Joseph and slandered him after rejection, that they urged him to betray his benefactor, or that they plotted to discredit him to the king.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r1.claim: The Prophet's choice to leave immediately and vindicate himself afterward was also sound: people may imitate these stories, and ordinary prisoners cannot know they will safely retain a chance to leave as Joseph did.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51#2/r2.claim: Joseph mentions the women collectively so that the Aziz's wife is included by implication without being named directly, a courteous and well-mannered formulation; the sentence ellipses a request to investigate them.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r1.claim: When the king's messenger arrives to summon Joseph, Joseph sends him back to ask the king about the women who cut their hands and about their situation.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains Joseph's delay as patient insistence on clearing his name before accepting royal favor, lest people forever remember the false accusation; Joseph also avoids offending the Aziz's household and honors the king's trust.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r2.claim: Joseph would not leave prison until his innocence was established before the king and it was clear he had been imprisoned without a crime.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r3.claim: In a report from Abū Hurayra, the Prophet calls Joseph son of four noble generations and says that, had he stayed in prison as long as Joseph, he would have answered the summons; he also recites the request to investigate the women.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhī's report from Abū Hurayra also has the Prophet praise Lot for relying on a strong support and say every prophet after him had a position of strength among his people.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r5.claim: Al-Bukhārī's report from Abū Hurayra repeats the prayer for mercy on Lot and the Prophet's statement that he would have answered the summons if imprisoned as long as Joseph; it adds that Abraham's request sought reassurance.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r6.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r6.claim: A further prophetic report calls Joseph patient and forbearing and says the Prophet would have answered the summons without seeking an excuse.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r7.claim: A similar report comes through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, a companion of Mālik, in al-Bukhārī's tafsir collection; it is his only report there.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r8.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī's version says the Prophet would have left quickly if summoned from prison and describes Joseph as forbearing and deliberate.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r9.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:50-51/r9.claim: Another report has the Prophet marvel at Joseph's patience in interpreting the cows before securing release, and at his delaying departure when the messenger arrived.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r10.claim: The word al-niswah is also read with a damma on its nun.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r6.claim: Joseph delayed leaving and asked the king to investigate the women so his innocence would be clear and an envious person could not use his imprisonment to defame him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r7.claim: The episode shows that one should work to dispel suspicions and avoid situations that invite accusation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r8.claim: The Prophet said that if he had been in Joseph's place and imprisoned for the same length of time, he would have answered the king's summons immediately.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r9.claim: Joseph's wording provokes a genuine inquiry; he refrains from accusing his former mistress out of generosity and proper etiquette, while affirming God's knowledge of their schemes and his innocence.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r1.claim: Joseph delays answering the king's summons and asks the messenger to return and inquire about the women who cut their hands, so his innocence is public before he leaves prison.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r2.claim: He wants to forestall enemies' slander and claims that his seven years in prison prove a grave crime; the episode shows that removing suspicion and avoiding accusatory situations are duties.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r3.claim: The Prophet is quoted marveling at Joseph's patience and generosity: the source says he himself would have required release before interpreting the king's dream and would have hurried out of prison.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#4/r4.claim: Joseph's gracious manners spared his former mistress: he mentions only the women who cut their hands; God knows their plot and will requite it.

QASHANI:12:49-51/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:49-51/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:49-51/r3.claim: Joseph's enthronement and the ruler's death signify the heart's succession to divine stewardship; marriage to the ruler's wife means the tranquil soul receives lawful benefits that support justice and knowledge.

QASHANI:12:49-51/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:49-51/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:49-51/r4.claim: The wife remaining a virgin signifies her balanced tranquility and the spirit's transcendence from the soul; she is the heart's wife because the heart governs her through spirit.

QASHANI:12:49-51/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:49-51/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:49-51/r5.claim: Stewardship signifies the heart's capacity to apprehend and preserve material particulars, unlike the spirit; the Holy Spirit grants this empowerment after annihilation, returning from unity to detail.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p283/r6.claim: Khaṭb is a consequential matter or affair, plural khuṭūb; a poetic line illustrates the word.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is quoted warning believers not to stand in places that invite suspicion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r10.claim: The author rejects al-Aziz as the referent of rabb; ‘their plotting’ refers specifically to the women under inquiry.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reportedly showed judges a written statement that his amputated leg was not cut for treachery or corruption, warding off suspicion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r3.claim: Joseph asked about the women rather than directly ordering a search because a question would prompt the king to investigate and expose the truth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r4.claim: Joseph’s question sought a full account that would make his innocence unmistakable and distinguish truth from falsehood.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r5.claim: Joseph’s restraint and generosity appear in his not naming the wife of al-Aziz despite her role in his imprisonment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r6.claim: Abu Haywa and Abu Bakr from Asim read al-niswah with a ḍamma on the nūn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r7.claim: A group read al-lāʾi, and both forms are plurals of allatī.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r8.claim: Joseph’s statement that God knows their plotting may testify to the scheme’s gravity and his innocence, threaten them, or imply divine recompense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows rabb to mean Joseph’s master, al-Aziz, as an appeal and reproach.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies omitted events: the messenger reported Joseph’s interpretation, and the king and court admired his insight and truthfulness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r2.claim: Impressed by Joseph’s interpretation and reputation for truth, the king ordered that he be brought to him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Joseph asked the king to investigate the women so he could determine whether the imprisonment was just.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya describes Joseph’s delay as patience and a demand to clear his name before accepting royal rank.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r5.claim: Joseph feared leaving prison and gaining favor while his religion and reputation remained unvindicated, so people would always regard him as the man who pursued his master’s wife.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Joseph waited to establish his innocence and forestall envious people using the imprisonment to lower his standing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p287/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari draws a principle that one should dispel suspicion and avoid places where accusations arise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r1.claim: The narrative omits the king hearing the women’s testimony and summoning Joseph; the speaker when they conversed may be the king or Joseph.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p291/r2.claim: Alternatively, Joseph may be the subject of ‘when he spoke with him,’ and the king admired his speech.

SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r1.claim: Most readers use kasra on the نون of النسوة; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission and Abu Haywa use damma, an uncommon reading.

SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:50/r2.claim: A reading has اللائي; both it and النسوة are plurals of التي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r1.claim: Impressed by Yusuf's interpretation, knowledge, insight, and good character, the king ordered him brought out of prison.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r2.claim: Yusuf refused release until the king and his people established his innocence and cleared his honor from the accusation that had unjustly imprisoned him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra's report in the two Sahih collections praises Yusuf's patience, saying the Prophet would have answered the caller if he had remained imprisoned as long.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r4.claim: Another report from Abu Hurayra says that if the Prophet were in Yusuf's place, he would have answered quickly and not sought an excuse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393#2/r5.claim: A mursal report through Ikrima marvels at Yusuf's patience and generosity: he would have insisted on release before interpreting the dream and would have hurried out when summoned, while Yusuf sought an exoneration.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r1.claim: Joseph refuses to leave prison until the accusation is examined, seeking public vindication so his imprisonment is not taken as proof of serious guilt.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r2.claim: Joseph courteously alludes to the women’s plotting instead of naming the wife of the ʿAzīz, showing modesty and generosity.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r3.claim: The question about what the king does not know is designed to spur investigation and secure acceptance of Joseph’s account once the truth is established.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r4.claim: Joseph’s insistence on clearing himself prevents the lasting shame and suspicion that could follow a prison sentence without public proof of innocence.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p53/r5.claim: Biqāʿī defines kīd as scheming to cause harm.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r1.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes baliya, to wear out or perish, from ibtalā, to be afflicted, in this lexical survey.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r2.claim: Several entries in the lexical survey are explained through an animal’s transformative contact with them.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r3.claim: Biqāʿī reads bāl as concern, thought, or worry, and explains “what is the matter?” through the idea of giving attention to another’s affair.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p54/r4.claim: Wābil means very heavy rain with forceful impact and large drops.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r1.claim: Biqāʿī says balā can affirm after a negative statement, unlike naʿam, and can answer a negative sentence even when no question was asked.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p55/r2.claim: Wabāl is severity and a bad outcome, associated with heaviness; the related wabīl can mean harsh punishment or an unpalatable pasture.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r1.claim: Ibil is a collective singular rather than a plural or collective noun, and the same form can mean clouds carrying rain.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p56/r2.claim: Biqāʿī explains the many camel-related derivatives through the transformative effect of contact, riding, and carrying.

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r4.claim: The Prophet said that, had he been in Joseph's place, he would have answered quickly rather than seek an excuse; al-Hakim authenticated this report.

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r5.claim: A second report from the Prophet prays for mercy on Joseph's forbearance and says he would have left prison quickly when summoned.

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r6.claim: The Prophet marvels that Joseph did not rush out when first summoned but waited to establish his innocence; he says he would have hurried to the door.

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r7.claim: Hasan transmits the Prophet's prayer for Joseph and says he would have answered quickly after long imprisonment.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r1.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v4p175/r1.claim: The poem contrasts the lover’s apparent gain and loss and asks for annihilation, abiding, and encounter; the author prays to be among those people.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p175/r2.claim: The king is Rayyan of Egypt; after the cupbearer returned with Joseph’s interpretation, the king admired his learning and wanted to honor him and hear him directly.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p175/r3.claim: Joseph told the envoy to return to his master and investigate what happened with the women who cut their hands at Zulaikha’s gathering.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p175/r4.claim: Joseph avoided naming his former mistress out of respect and caution about her schemes; he trusted the other women to admit she solicited him and he resisted.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r5.speaker: العلماء
BURSEVI:v4p175/r5.claim: Scholars say Joseph delayed leaving prison until the king established his innocence, especially before the Aziz, displaying patience and preventing jealous people from defaming him.

BURSEVI:v4p175/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p175/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p175/r6.claim: His conduct teaches the need to dispel suspicion and avoid places that invite it; a hadith says believers should not enter suspicious situations.

BURSEVI:v4p179/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p179/r1.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v4p179/r1.claim: The king first summoned Joseph only for dream interpretation; after seeing his integrity, patience, resolve, judgment, and restraint, he summoned him again as an intimate.

BURSEVI:v4p179/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p179/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p179/r2.claim: The king calls Joseph trustworthy and high-ranking from that day; ‘today’ marks when these qualities begin, not a later period.

BURSEVI:v4p179/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p179/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p179/r3.claim: Joseph left prison after bidding its people farewell and praying for them; the account says news reached the prisoners before the public and records an inscription calling prison a trial-house and grave for the living.

BURSEVI:v4p179/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p179/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p179/r4.claim: Joseph washed, changed into new clothes, and was escorted to the king; al-Taysīr reports seventy chamberlains and seventy mounts were sent to the prison.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r1.claim: On the first reading, reserving full knowledge of their guile to God adds suspense and urges the king to investigate; the sentence completes Joseph's request to inquire.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r10.claim: Abu Haywa and Abu Bakr in one transmission from Asim read النِّسوة with a rounded ḍamma on nūn; another group reads اللائي with yā, like the plural اللاء.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r2.claim: On the second reading, the sentence sums up the case: if God knows the women plotted, Joseph is necessarily innocent. The third can serve either function and may stir the king to punish them, though that seems ill-matched to Joseph's nobility.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud relates the Prophet's admiration for Joseph's nobility and patience: he said he would have required release before interpreting the dream and would have hurried out when summoned from prison, unlike Joseph's patient insistence on clarifying his innocence.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r4.claim: One explanation of the Prophet's prayer is that Joseph chose a concession rather than the higher resolve: he put clearing his name ahead of God's right to convey monotheism and the message.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r5.claim: Al-Tibi reads the prayer as a respectful, conventional rebuke, like telling an honored person 'may God forgive you' while querying his answer.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r6.claim: Another view says clearing his name served God's cause too: once the accusation was removed, Joseph's later teaching would be accepted; avoiding situations that invite suspicion is obligatory.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r7.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r7.claim: Muslim's report from Anas says the Prophet, walking with a wife, called out to a passerby that she was his wife; when the man said he would never suspect him, the Prophet explained that Satan circulates through humans like blood, illustrating the need to dispel suspicion.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari documented with judges that his leg was lost to frost on a journey, not crime, and displayed their letters in each town to prevent suspicion; Joseph may likewise have feared that silence would invite detractors to undermine his message.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257#2/r9.claim: Al-Alusi rejects Ibn Atiyya's suggestion that 'my lord' means the Aziz as in Joseph's earlier statement about his master, and rejects changing the antecedent of 'their guile' to women generally.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r1.claim: After hearing the full and precise interpretation, the king asks for Joseph because of his knowledge and virtue, which disclose what only God could make known.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r2.claim: When the messenger who had been Joseph's fellow prisoner arrives to say the king wants him, Joseph tells him to return to his master, the king.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r3.claim: Rather than explicitly ordering an investigation, Joseph asks the king what happened with the women; a question provokes the king's curiosity and concern for what he does not know, whereas a direct request might seem bold and be refused.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r4.claim: Joseph omits the Aziz's wife, the principal party, out of courtesy and magnanimity, which moves her to confess; another explanation is that he feared her continued plotting, while expecting the other women to tell the truth.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r5.claim: By mentioning the women's cutting their hands without directly accusing them of seduction, Joseph is tactful, guards against their taking offense, and alludes to the events through his lord's knowledge of their guile.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p257/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers three readings of 'my Lord knows their guile': it is too great for anyone but God to know; God knows they plotted and that Joseph is innocent; or it is a veiled warning that God knows and will punish them.

ELMALILI:12:50/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:50/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:50/r1.claim: After hearing the cupbearer's account, the king recognizes Yusuf's learning and virtue and orders that he be brought from prison.

ELMALILI:12:50/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:50/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:50/r2.claim: Yusuf refuses to leave immediately and asks for a public inquiry into the women who cut their hands, so his innocence and unjust imprisonment become clear to others; God already knows the truth.

ELMALILI:12:50/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:50/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:50/r3.claim: Yusuf avoids naming the chief's wife and has remained unshaken through years in prison, showing exceptional restraint and dignity.

ELMALILI:12:50/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:50/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:50/r4.claim: The king appreciates Yusuf's concern and personally summons and interrogates the women to investigate the matter.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r1.claim: The king orders Yusuf brought after hearing the interpretation; he addresses his court to send someone, and the narrative leaves the dispatch implicit before the messenger arrives.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r2.claim: Yusuf refuses to leave prison before clearing his name: otherwise his interpretive success could look like special pleading, leaving the false accusation alive and inviting later envy; vindicating reputation is a legitimate aim.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r3.claim: He asks that the king be questioned about the women to reopen the case from its beginning; an unjustly imprisoned person should patiently remain until acquitted so he appears before the ruler without suspicion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r4.claim: The Prophet said that had he remained in prison as long as Yusuf, he would have answered the king's summons; the narrator explains this means the king's messenger after Yusuf asked for an inquiry.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r5.claim: Yusuf's question is meant to prompt the king to investigate, not to obtain information; the king already knows the matter, as in Q 78:1.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p288#2/r6.claim: Asking about all the women rather than naming the Aziz's wife makes disclosure easier, since the king might hesitate to probe a powerful courtier's household; the public banquet story and the women's testimony make this concise approach effective.

TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r3.claim: A report says Joseph stumbled three times: when he desired her and was imprisoned, when he asked the cupbearer to mention him and forgot his Lord, and when he said the brothers were thieves.

TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r4.claim: The report conflicts with verses describing God’s election and purification of Joseph and Satan’s lack of access; its alleged grave sins cannot fit his status as a truthful benefactor, and similar reports are unreliable.

TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r1.claim: Joseph’s later wording that he had not betrayed her in his absence, along with the women’s role in the affair, suggests they invited him toward the wife and shared the story with her.

TABATABAI:12:35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:35/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:35/r6.claim: Later evidence shows the wife may have misled her husband into doubting Joseph’s innocence; she may have arranged or ordered prison both to protect herself and to punish him into obedience.

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r1.speaker: سماعة
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r1.claim: A report in al-Ayyashi identifies the Aziz as Joseph’s lord in the instruction to return to him and ask about the women.

TABATABAI:12:43-57/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r1.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r1.claim: A report transmitted in al-Ayyashi says the Prophet admired Joseph’s patience and would have required release before interpreting the king’s dream.

TABATABAI:12:43-57/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r2.claim: The author rejects the report because it either impugns Joseph’s sound strategy or suggests the Prophet would fail to show the patience he praised.

TABATABAI:12:43-57/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r3.claim: Joseph wanted vindication, an end to the women’s pursuit, and a position from which to administer justice, not mere release; interpreting the dream first enabled the summons, and insisting on inquiry led to the king’s personal appointment.

TABATABAI:12:43-57/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57/r4.claim: This was excellent statecraft: the king and officials saw Joseph’s patience, resolve, knowledge, and sound judgment, supporting his rise and public service.

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r5.claim: After the messenger reports the interpretation and advice, the king orders Joseph brought to him; the account omits that transition for brevity.

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r6.claim: The king is alarmed by the predicted famine and impressed by Joseph’s practical wisdom, so he summons him to speak and understand the advice more fully.

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r7.claim: The summons means release from prison for an audience, not a temporary transfer back to prison; Joseph was free to request a just inquiry before appearing.

TABATABAI:12:50-51/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r1.claim: Joseph speaks courteously: he avoids naming the Aziz’s wife, asks about the women collectively, and seeks an investigation that proves his complete innocence.

TABATABAI:12:50-51/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r2.claim: His only complaint is to God in saying that his Lord knows the women’s plot; repeating Lord in his request and this statement subtly identifies the Lord addressed to the messenger.

TABATABAI:12:50-51/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r3.claim: The double use of my Lord in the request and in the statement about the women undercuts the claim that Joseph earlier called the Aziz his lord.

TABATABAI:12:50-51/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:50-51/r4.claim: Ma bal asks what grave affair caused the women to cut their hands; the question prompts the king to recognize their infatuation and the exceptional difficulty of resisting them.

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Context implies the messenger reported Joseph's interpretation to the king, who was impressed and immediately summoned him; the narrative omits these steps.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The messenger would expect a prisoner who had endured years in jail to be glad of release and leave at once.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph insisted that the episode used to imprison him be investigated before he accepted release.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God's knowledge of the conspiracy assured Joseph, while an investigation would clear him and prevent later blame.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph would not accept release or closeness to the king on a temporary benefit of doubt; he prioritized clearing his name and trusted his truthfulness and God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r1.claim: After hearing Joseph’s accurate interpretation, the king requests him; by divine inspiration Joseph knows he will rise to high office, yet declines immediate release until the suspicion is cleared and his innocence and chastity publicly established.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r2.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r2.claim: The Prophet praised Joseph’s patience and maturity in the trial of prison.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:50/r3.claim: Joseph acts with exemplary courtesy, protecting his benefactor Aziz’s honor by asking for an inquiry into the women who cut their hands without naming Aziz’s wife as the cause of his imprisonment.

QIRAAT-ER:12:50:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:50:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:50:15#1/r1.claim: Eliding hamza from fasʾalhu produces a lighter phonological form, also canonical.

QIRAAT-ER:12:50:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:50:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:50:4#1/r1.claim: A hamza variant supplies a different phonological realization of the imperative, also canonical.

STUDYQURAN:12:50/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r1.claim: After hearing Joseph’s interpretation, the king asked the messenger to bring Joseph to him.

STUDYQURAN:12:50/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r2.claim: Joseph sought to clear himself by asking the king to confront the women who had cut their hands.

STUDYQURAN:12:50/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:50/r3.claim: The messenger conveyed Joseph’s inquiry, and the king gathered the women.
